newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent Group diesel diffs firm on draw.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent Group diesel diffs firm on draw.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent spot low sulphur diesel fuel differentials firmed in Group Three on steady demand and a draw in distillate stocks, traders said.

Distillate inventories in the PADD II Midwest market were drawn down 2.77 million barrels in the week ended October 18, the American Petroleum Institute said in its weekly inventory survey released late Tuesday.
Gasoline differentials also found support from API's estimate gasoline inventories in the region were drawn down by 5.24 million barrels due to refinery turnarounds, traders said.

A court hearing was scheduled for Wednesday in Chicago, where the Illinois Attorney General is seeking a temporary restraining order that would idle Clark Refining and Marketing Co's 80,515 barrel per day Blue Island, Ill., refinery until the company can demonstrate it can be operated safely.

An explosion and fire rocked the refinery over the weekend and idled a 6,400 barrel per day alkylation unit. Last year, another explosion killed two workers, and in a separate incident a release of hydrofluoric acid floated over a nearby high school, making more than two dozen students ill.
The refiner defended its safety record since the fatal accident, and called efforts to close the facility "unwarranted and unjustified."
Group Three low sulphur diesel was talked 3.0/3.25 cents a gallon over NYMEX November heating oil, with high sulphur 2.0 cents over.
Chicago low sulphur diesel was talked unchanged at 1.50/1.25 cents under the print, with high sulphur firming to 3.0 cents under.

Traders said some high sulphur barrels may have found their way through the Buckeye pipeline system to New York-area markets, where heating oil stocks are 18.84 million barrels below last year's levels.
